title: Branch Banking Bulletin: The Owner's Election on ATM and One-Time Debit Card Items
content:
The debit overdraft election on a Personal Checking account governs only cash machine withdrawals and one-time debit card purchases. Checks, direct debits and recurring debit card payments are unaffected by it.

**Clauses.**

1. Opting in requires the owner's own affirmative consent, given by the owner rather than recorded on the owner's behalf. What the owner states in the contact is the authority for that consent.
2. Opting in is available only on a tier that offers discretionary overdraft coverage, judged from the tier the account carries.
3. Opting out can be requested at any time on any tier and takes effect when it is recorded.
4. A new election applies to transactions authorized after it is recorded and never re-prices items already paid or declined; an opt-out does not refund charges already assessed.
5. Recording the election already in force changes nothing and writes nothing.

**Basis Q and A.**

*An owner of Access Checking asks to opt in.* That tier offers no discretionary overdraft coverage, so opting in is not available on it.

*An owner opts out after three items were paid into overdraft yesterday.* The election takes effect from when it is recorded and governs later authorizations; the three charges already assessed stand under their own basis.

*An owner already opted out asks to opt out.* The election in force is already that one, so nothing changes and nothing is recorded.
